Four Years of Creating for a Community

I’m 20 years old, and for the past four years, I’ve been creating visual designs for the Computer Science Society of the Department of Computing and Informatics at City College of Calamba. What started as a passion for designing has grown into a meaningful role, where I now serve as the Publicity Materials Head (PubMat Head), leading the team responsible for bringing the organization’s visual identity to life.

From event posters and announcements to tribute cards and merchandise, I enjoy turning ideas into designs that communicate, connect, and leave an impression.

My design approach focuses on clear visual hierarchy, expressive typography, and thoughtful layouts that capture the right mood for every occasion. For me, every design is more than just visuals—it’s a way to tell a story and give a community its own identity.

What I can do

Everything in my portfolio falls into these areas, and I keep adding new ones as I learn.

Event posters

Posters and series for talks, workshops, competitions, and general assemblies.

Social media pubmats

Feed-ready announcements and reminders sized for Facebook and Instagram.

Tribute cards

Photo-based greetings for birthdays, graduations, and well-deserved shout-outs.

Infographics

Explainers on topics like vaccination and phishing, laid out so dense information stays easy to read.

UI design

App and website screens, from sign-in pages to menus and analytics dashboards.

Logos and merch

Logo marks and shirt layouts made for print and pre-order.

Promo ads

Bold product visuals, like a pizza pocket ad, built to make people hungry or curious.

Film direction

Directed the short film “An Inconvenient Love” and designed its poster.

How a design comes together

  1. Understand

    I start with what the design is for, who will see it, and what it should make them feel or do.

  2. Sketch

    I pick the focal point, the type, and the mood before opening any layers.

  3. Craft

    I build the layout, refine the details, and check that it reads at thumbnail size.

  4. Share

    I export the final design in the right size and share it online, ready to post.
